Activity per party

Source: R/context-anchor.R
party_activity.Rd

Counts turns by the speaker's party at the time, by parliament and chamber.

Usage

party_activity(
  party_id = NULL,
  parliament_id = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  chamber_venue = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

party_id

Filter on party_id_at_time: whole numbers or in_range(). List the parties with get_parties().

parliament_id

Filter on the sitting's parliament_id: whole numbers or in_range().

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

chamber_venue

Filter on the turn's chamber_venue: whole numbers or in_range().

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per party at the time, parliament and chamber, ordered by parliament_id, chamber and party_at_time, and columns party_id_at_time, party_at_time, parliament_id, chamber, n_members, n_turns, n_speeches, n_interjections and n_words. Zero rows if nothing matches; a lazy table (in no set order) if collect = FALSE.

Details

The metrics n_turns, n_speeches and n_words are defined as in member_activity(); n_interjections is its n_interjections_made. n_members counts the speaking members: the distinct PHIDs with at least one turn for that party in that parliament and chamber.

Party. Each turn is assigned the party its speaker belonged to on the sitting date (v_party_at_time), so a member who changed party is counted under each party for the turns made in it. Turns without a party at the time (presiding officers, speakers with no PHID, and members with no party recorded for the date) are not counted. Party lineage is not followed.

See also

member_activity(), parliament_summary(), add_party()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
party_activity()
#> # A tibble: 36 × 9
#>    party_id_at_time party_at_time        parliament_id chamber n_members n_turns
#>               <int> <chr>                        <int> <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1                1 Australian Labor Pa…             1 house          10      24
#>  2               27 Free Trade                       1 house           2       5
#>  3               48 Protectionist Party              1 house           9      55
#>  4                1 Australian Labor Pa…             7 senate          7      25
#>  5               39 Nationalist Party                7 senate          6      25
#>  6               13 Australian Democrats            33 senate          1       1
#>  7                1 Australian Labor Pa…            33 senate         14      47
#>  8                4 Liberal Party of Au…            33 senate         11      19
#>  9               60 National Party of A…            33 senate          2       2
#> 10                1 Australian Labor Pa…            36 house          22      51
#> # ℹ 26 more rows
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_speeches <dbl>, n_interjections <dbl>, n_words <dbl>
party_activity(party_id = 1, chamber = "house")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 9
#>   party_id_at_time party_at_time         parliament_id chamber n_members n_turns
#>              <int> <chr>                         <int> <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1                1 Australian Labor Par…             1 house          10      24
#> 2                1 Australian Labor Par…            36 house          22      51
#> 3                1 Australian Labor Par…            40 house          22      28
#> 4                1 Australian Labor Par…            47 house          37      75
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: n_speeches <dbl>, n_interjections <dbl>, n_words <dbl>
db_disconnect()
